basis.governing_question: How can Metalúrgica Norte cut conversion cost across its six plants in Portugal and Spain and put the improvements in place in every plant?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish where conversion cost per part arises in each plant and size the improvements that would reduce it.

gate.label: Initiative go/no-go
gate.decision: Go or no-go on the sized improvements, and which plant pilots them first?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Carry out the approved improvements at a pilot plant, roll them out to the other plants, and track savings.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the final results and the running improvements in all six plants?

workstreams.name: Baseline: first two plants
workstreams.answers: Where does conversion cost per part sit in the first two plants diagnosed, and what causes it?
activities: Build a conversion cost per part baseline from plant data
Observe the lines and interview the people who run them
Analyze the losses that raise cost per part by line

workstreams.name: Baseline: third plant
workstreams.answers: Where does conversion cost per part sit in the third plant diagnosed, and what causes it?
activities: Build the third plant's cost per part baseline
Observe the lines and interview the people who run them
Analyze the losses that raise cost per part by line

workstreams.name: Baseline: other three plants
workstreams.answers: Where does conversion cost per part sit in the other three plants, judged from their data?
activities: Collect cost and operational data from the other plants
Apply the drivers found in the first two plants to the data
Check the estimates with each Plant Director

workstreams.name: Improvement sizing by plant
workstreams.answers: Which improvements cut conversion cost per part by a measurable amount in each plant, and by how much?
activities: Identify improvements for each plant's cost drivers
Size each improvement's cost per part reduction by plant
Compare plants as pilot candidates for the go/no-go

workstreams.name: Pilot plant improvements
workstreams.answers: Do the approved improvements show savings in the cost data at the pilot plant?
activities: Prepare the approved changes at the pilot plant
Put the changes live after the readiness workshop
Read savings in the plant's cost data against baseline

workstreams.name: Savings tracking by plant
workstreams.answers: What conversion cost per part does each plant show against its baseline once the improvements run?
activities: Set up a cost per part tracker against each baseline
Update the tracker from cost data as each plant goes live
Compare each plant's cost per part with its baseline

workstreams.name: Plant rollout, wave 1
workstreams.answers: How are the improvements put in place in the first wave of the other plants?
activities: Adapt the changes tested at the pilot plant to each plant
Train the plant teams and put the changes live in wave 1
Track wave 1 results in each plant's cost data

workstreams.name: Plant rollout, wave 2
workstreams.answers: How are the improvements put in place in the remaining plants so all six plants are running them?
activities: Adjust the rollout approach using wave 1 results
Train the plant teams and put the changes live in wave 2
Confirm the improvements run in all six plants

deliverables.name: Conversion cost per part baseline: first two plants
Conversion cost per part baseline: third plant
Conversion cost per part estimate: other three plants
Go/no-go pack: baselines, sizing and pilot plant options
Pilot plant change plan and readiness checklist
Go-live record for the pilot plant
Pilot plant savings report against baseline
Conversion cost per part tracker against baselines
Final readout pack: results and running improvements
Wave 1 training and go-live record for each plant
Wave 1 results against baseline by plant
Wave 2 training and go-live record for each plant
Record of improvements running in all six plants

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Agree access to plant data and people
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Which two plants open their cost data and staff first for the baselines?
agenda: Present the diagnostic approach and the plant baselines due by week 5
Align on the cost data and staff time each plant must provide
Decide which two plants open their data and staff first

events.label: Workshop 1: plant baselines
events.purpose: Review plant cost baselines and estimates
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Which plants should the go/no-go pack put forward as pilot options?
agenda: Present baselines for three plants and estimates for the other three
Review where conversion cost per part arises in each plant
Decide which plants the go/no-go pack puts forward as pilot options

events.label: Initiative go/no-go
events.purpose: Decide go/no-go and the pilot plant
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Go or no-go on the sized improvements, and which plant pilots them first?
agenda: Present the sized improvements by plant and the go/no-go pack
Review baselines, sizing and the pilot plant options
Decide go or no-go and which plant pilots first

events.label: Workshop 2: pilot readiness
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Go or no-go on taking the pilot plant live under the change plan?
agenda: Present the pilot plant change plan and readiness checklist
Review checklist status before the pilot plant goes live
Decide whether the pilot plant goes live under the change plan

events.label: Check-in: pilot results
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Confirm the tracker and pilot savings as the measure for wave 2 results?
agenda: Present the pilot go-live record and savings report against baseline
Review the conversion cost per part tracker against the baselines
Confirm how wave 2 results will be measured against baseline

events.label: Workshop 3: wave 1 results
events.purpose: Review wave 1 results before final readout
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Go or no-go on starting wave 2 in the remaining plants, given wave 1 results?
agenda: Present wave 1 results against baseline and go-live records by plant
Review pilot savings and the tracker as the basis for the final readout
Decide whether wave 2 starts in the remaining plants

events.label: Final readout
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Approve the final results and the running improvements in all six plants?
agenda: Present the final readout pack with results by plant
Review the record of improvements running in all six plants
Decide whether to approve the results and running improvements

architect_notes: The brief gives no engagement length, so the 25 to 29 weeks are an estimate from the work sizing, not a stated length.
Implementation takes the middle of a 16 to 24 week estimate; a 12-week pilot plant and 6-week waves would push it to the top.
Diagnostic assumes three representative plants are diagnosed on the floor and the other three extended from data; which plants is open.
No Measurement phase: results tracking runs inside Implementation, so post-launch tracking beyond the last wave needs the partner's decision.

sub_questions.question: Where does conversion cost per part sit in each plant today, and what drives it?
Which improvements, sized per plant, cut conversion cost per part by a measurable amount in every plant?
Do the approved improvements show savings in the cost data at the pilot plant?
How are the improvements put in place in the other plants so they are running in all six plants?
What conversion cost per part does each plant show against its baseline once the improvements run?

drivers.evidence: six plants in Portugal and Spain

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Site diagnosed on the floor (cost baseline, line observation, loss analysis)

phases.why: Three plants diagnosed two at a time, the other three extended from data; above typical 3-6 weeks because three plants need two rounds.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: Pilot site: changes made and savings shown in the cost data
Rollout wave of up to 3 sites

phases.why: Pilot plant, then two rollout waves for the other five plants in sequence; above the typical 8-16 weeks because the work adds up.

sizing.levers: Running the two rollout waves side by side would cut the most; diagnosing two plants instead of three saves about two weeks.
